author.heading: About Hermann Hesse
author.bio: Hermann Hesse wrote Demian, Siddhartha and Steppenwolf, novels concerned with identity, inner conflict and spiritual development. Born in Germany, he became a Swiss citizen and received the 1946 Nobel Prize in Literature.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Sinclair has sent Demian a painting of a bird emerging from a globe. The reply compares the egg to a world that must be broken to make birth possible, then names Abraxas; its setting is a novel about the development of Sinclair’s identity.
